messages.subject: Re: "Thurstonian IRT-model for binary forced choice data" - computable in lavaan?
messages.subject_clean: "Thurstonian IRT-model for binary forced choice data" - computable in lavaan?
messages.body_plain:
On 12/31/2012 12:08 PM, Henning Bumann wrote:
> Hello everyone,
>
> I'm fairly new to structural equation modeling in general and do not
> know the lavaan package very well so far.
>
> My goal is to fit an "Thurstonian IRT-Model" to binary forced choice
> questionnaire data and I would like to know if this can already be done
> in lavaan

I don't think so. It would seem (and this is also reflected in the Mplus
syntax) that these models rely on the so-called 'theta' parameterization
for categorical variables. lavaan currently (0.5-11) only supports the
'delta' parameterization. In the 'theta' parameterization, the residual
errors of the (binary) indicators can be estimated (if they are
identified; be default, they are fixed to 1), while in the 'delta'
parameterization, they are never estimated (they are a function of other
model parameters).

But I'm working on the theta parameterization, and it should be
available in 0.5-12. Once we have this in place, I believe lavaan will
be able to fit these Thurstonian IRT models.

But a much nicer approach (IMHO) would be to have a dedicated function
(say, thurstonianIRT()) where there is no need to force a SEM
parameterization upon a non-SEM model, but where we fit the needed
parameters directly.

Yves.

for the quadratic term: simply square the coefficients:

quad =~ 0*t03 + 1*t04 + 4*t05 + 9*t06 + 16*t07 + 25*t08 + 36*t09 +

for the cubic term: use 0^3, 1^3, 2^3, ...

Yves.

On 01/21/2013 02:10 PM, Ruud wrote:
> Dear users and friends,
>
> I try to statistically compare two indirect effects in the latent model
> with two mediators.
> If the first indirect effect is the product of path a and path b (i.e.,
> ab) and the second is the product of path c and path d (i.e., cd), how
> could I compare these effects (e.g., ab - cd) and test for statistical
> significance (whether the difference is different from zero) using the
> bootstrapping method?

See the lavaan paper (http://www.jstatsoft.org/v48/i02/) section 7.4 how
to define labels, and how the ':=' operator can be used to construct
arbitrary functions of parameters. If you have labeled some parameters
as 'a','b','c,' and 'd', you can define a new variable as follows:

diff.effect := a*b - c*d

and if you request se="bootstrap", you will get a bootstrap standard
error for this effect, and confidence intervals when your request
parameterEstimates(fit).

I also try the phantom model approach (Macho &
> Ledermann, 2011), but do not know how to tell the program to report the
> total effect of a phantom model.

No need for phantom variables, but if you need to create them, use

phantom ~= 0

Hope this helps,

Yves.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Yonghao,

It might be a problem of factor indeterminacy. Imagine that you have one solution with factor loadings of 0.7, 0.6, and 0.5. The similar solution could be one with factor loadings of -0.7, -0.6, and -0.5 (with exactly the same fit). Since the factor means are implied from those factor loadings, the directions between two means could be reversed. What you could do is to set a constraint on factor loadings

script <- "f1 =~ load1*x1 + load2*x2 + load3*x3
load1 > 0"

or to use marker-variable method to make sure that loadings are positive.

Sunthud

messages.subject: Re: Omega hierarchical in lavaan?

messages.body_plain:
To the best of my knowledge, lavaan only used the Delta/marginal parameterization for categorical endogenous variables, which constrains the indicators' error variance to 1 (estimating the underlying variable's variance instead), thus making e1-e30 "non-free". You'll have to pretend your indicators are continuous for the syntax to work; in such cases, you might want to estimate the polychoric correlations first, and use them as input into lavaan.

Best,

Alex

messages.subject: p value calculation for bootstrapped parameters
messages.subject_clean: p value calculation for bootstrapped parameters
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

when using se="boot" and retrieving parameters with parameterEstimates, the type of bootstrapped CIs can be adjusted using boot.ci.type.
The p value that is reported, however, is independent of that last parameter (and it does not seem to be the percentile bootstrapped p).

Consider following parameters (bootstrapped with B=1000):

  label   est      se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
1    b4 0.033   0.023 1.484  0.138    0.000    0.086
2     S 0.453 766.930 0.001  1.000    0.054    1.081
3    l1 0.000   0.002 0.000  1.000    0.000    0.004

- The lower 95% CI of the first row is zero, so the p value should be around .05
- The CI of the second row is clearly above zero, but due to the enormous bootstrapped SE the p value is 1.

I have two questions:
1. How is the SE and p value calculated in the bootstrap case?
2. Is there any argument *not* to use the percentile p value, which would treat the second row as "significant"? What is the difference between these two approaches?

Thanks,
Felix
